import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

It didn't overwrite anything, it's registered as `research:202611/explicit_micro_tasks/explicit_micro_tasks.md` (`file:explicit:53855172cabdbaef8b53ac73`), and the commit is declared and will be made when this turn ends.

**Structure:** the file opens with the title, a research-query summary of your request, the infographic (`explicit_micro_tasks_infographic.png`, which is in the folder), then `## Bottom line`. Below that, the requirement adjustments table now comes right after "What every report agreed on", so your "what would you change" question is answered early. The lead's details about who wrote it and the restated question moved to a new "About this report" section just before Sources. Headings are no longer numbered. Where a heading had a parenthetical or code (for example "(one real adjustment)" or the `##` request), that text now opens the section instead.

**Diagrams:** all three proposals are placed, each with one sentence pointing to it. The diagram manifest was ready and its source matched the lead's report. None were left out.
- `capture-dot-contexts` → `#figure-capture-dot-contexts`, after the list in "Capture and editing".
- `close-card-routing` → `#figure-close-card-routing`, right after the close card's **When.** paragraph.
- `keep-open-subtree` → `#figure-keep-open-subtree`, after the **Writes.** list.

The lead's own Figure 1 is kept as it was, so the file has 4 Mermaid diagrams. The two grk images registered under the lead (`figure-roundtrip.png`, `figure-classify.png`) are not embedded, because the lead's report never embedded them.

**Links and checks:**
- **Section references:** the lead's "§3", "§6", "§7.3" and "§9" pointed at section numbers that no longer exist, so they are now links to the matching sections.
- **One corrected reference:** the lead's "see §12", written about cdx's full staged close, now links to "What I did not adopt and from whom". That's the only section that discusses cdx's staged close, so it was almost certainly a typo for §13; the lead's §12 is the adjustments table.
- **Kept as written:** references to sections of other documents, such as `docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.x and "cdx §10".
- **Link check:** all 17 in-document links resolve when checked with pandoc. The lead's report has no external URLs, and the only relative link is the infographic.
- **Completeness check:** every other line of the lead's report appears unchanged.

**One rendering issue I left alone:** row A6 of the adjustments table has `[[#^new|Alias]]` inside code. The PDF (pandoc) shows it correctly, but GitHub will likely treat that `|` as a column break and the row will look broken there. Escaping it as `\|` would put a stray backslash in the PDF, so I kept the lead's text unchanged.
